clue.text: After excluding two unknowns, group of stars party

indicators.note: excluding means leaving something out, so once those letters are removed the rest remains

blocks.note: a galaxy is a vast group of stars
x and y are the usual unknowns in algebra

explanation.surface: A galaxy, minus a couple of mysteries, throws a party.
explanation.walkthrough: Crosswords borrow the algebra letters x, y and z for 'unknowns'; here two of them come off GALAXY to leave GALA.
explanation.definitionFit: A gala is a festive social occasion or celebration, which is a kind of party.

clue.text: 150 may riot over European money for weapon

indicators.note: to riot is to run wild, so the letters of the neighbouring word are thrown into disorder
in a down clue, one piece sitting over another is simply written above it, so first comes before second

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
the öre is a small coin of Sweden, Denmark and Norway

explanation.surface: A hundred and fifty people might riot over euros, as a reason to take up arms.
explanation.walkthrough: '150' looks like a count of rioters but is Roman CL; the öre is the Scandinavian coin worth a hundredth of a krona.
explanation.definitionFit: A claymore is a large two-edged Scottish broadsword, a type of weapon.

clue.text: Successful in Australia, Kelly's record is revoked

indicators.note: revoking undoes or turns back a decision, so the pieces are read from end to start

blocks.note: a log is a written record

explanation.surface: An Australian called Kelly did well, but then her record was cancelled.
explanation.walkthrough: Ned Kelly was the notorious 19th-century Australian bushranger; his NED and LOG are written backwards together.
explanation.definitionFit: Golden can mean very successful or flourishing, as in a golden era or golden boy.

clue.text: Before Conservative Party's finished, Johnson finally quit and gave up

indicators.note: the setter reads 'before Y, X' as X put ahead of Y, so the second-named item leads
finally points at the very end of the name it follows, keeping only its closing letter
something that has quit has left, so that letter goes out of the word

blocks.note: CON is short for the Conservative Party

explanation.surface: Boris Johnson resigned in defeat before his party's time in government was over.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter confirmed this parse, reading 'before Y, X' as X ahead of Y, so the party comes ahead of the single-letter Conservative; many solvers found that order hard.
explanation.definitionFit: To concede is to admit defeat or surrender something, so conceded is a past-tense synonym for gave up.

clue.text: Various nuts lacking individual taste

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters are scrambled into a new order
lacking means going without, so one letter is taken out first

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one, a single individual

explanation.surface: An assortment of nuts with no distinctive flavour of its own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nuts' and 'taste' look like a snack review; nuts is the scramble signal and taste is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To savour is to taste and enjoy something slowly, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Overseas characters stuff up

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading from the bottom to the top

blocks.note: to stuff yourself is to sate your appetite

explanation.surface: Foreign people stuff themselves full.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overseas characters' sounds like foreign people but means letters of a foreign alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Eta is a letter of the Greek alphabet, so etas are characters used abroad in Greece.

clue.text: Boycott gets 50 and left balls in bag

indicators.note: items placed in something go inside it, here within the word for boycott

blocks.note: two round letters O look like balls

explanation.surface: Geoffrey Boycott scores a fifty and leaves the balls in his kit bag.
explanation.walkthrough: Geoffrey Boycott was a famous Yorkshire and England cricket batsman, so the surface is about cricket; here boycott is simply a ban.
explanation.definitionFit: A balloon is an inflatable bag of thin rubber or fabric filled with air or gas.

clue.text: They say sitcom family cuppa has majestic quality

indicators.note: what people say is spoken, so the words are judged by their sound rather than spelling

blocks.note: The Royle Family is a British TV sitcom; a cuppa is a cup of tea

explanation.surface: Rumour has it a TV sitcom family's cup of tea is fit for a king.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royle Family was a British sitcom about a couch-bound Manchester family; a cuppa is British slang for a cup of tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Royalty can mean the status or dignity of a monarch, a regal or majestic character.

clue.text: Knight undressed noblewoman

indicators.note: stripping off the outer layer leaves only the inside, so the first and last letters go

explanation.surface: A knight strips off in front of a noblewoman.
explanation.walkthrough: Knight is not a knight in armour but Gladys Knight, of Gladys Knight and the Pips; her first name loses its outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A lady is a woman of noble rank, the title held by a peeress or a knight's wife.

clue.text: Lied about Conservative promises being tasteful

indicators.note: about suggests something turned around and moved, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
IOUs are written promises to pay

explanation.surface: A Tory lied about his promises showing good taste.
explanation.walkthrough: Tasteful here means full of taste, as food is, rather than showing refinement.
explanation.definitionFit: Delicious food has a delightful flavour; the clue uses tasteful in the literal sense of full of flavour.

clue.text: White meat course partially cooked

indicators.note: partially means only in part, so the word is used without its final letter
cooking transforms ingredients, so the remaining letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A white-meat dish served half-cooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'White meat' reads as one phrase, but White is the definition and meat starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambrusco is a sparkling Italian wine, usually red but also made as a white.

clue.text: New? My mistake sending back old club

indicators.note: sending back returns something the way it came, so the letters are read in the other direction

blocks.note: what you say when you slip up

explanation.surface: A golfer admits a blunder and returns an antique club.
explanation.walkthrough: The spoon was an old wooden golf club, roughly a modern three-wood.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoon was the historical name of a lofted wooden golf club, now called a three-wood.

clue.text: Oscar winner shockingly hits man's face

indicators.note: shockingly suggests something jolted out of shape, so the letters are jumbled
a face is the front, so only the opening letter of the word is kept

explanation.surface: An Oscar winner shocks everyone by slapping a man across the face.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls Will Smith slapping Chris Rock at the 2022 Oscars, shortly before winning Best Actor; the clue's description is also the answer's own story.
explanation.definitionFit: Will Smith won the Academy Award for Best Actor for King Richard in 2022.

clue.text: Fair river in China

indicators.note: one thing sitting in another is placed inside it

blocks.note: the Oder is a river of central Europe
Cockney rhyming slang: china plate, mate

explanation.surface: A pleasant river runs through China.
explanation.walkthrough: China is not the country: in Cockney rhyming slang 'china plate' means mate, a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair and moderate both mean middling or reasonable, neither very good nor bad.

clue.text: Big actor briefly dropping hot containers

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the first name is reduced to its initial
dropping something lets it fall away, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: Tom Hanks starred in the film Big
H is the hot tap abbreviation

explanation.surface: A burly actor sheds a few hot water bottles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big' reads as large, but it is the 1988 film Big, whose star was Tom Hanks.
explanation.definitionFit: Tanks are large receptacles for holding liquid or gas, so they are containers.

clue.text: In Sweden, I was knocking back drink

indicators.note: in says the letters are found inside the run of words that follows
knocking back sends something backwards, so the found letters run right to left

blocks.note: the letters run across these words

explanation.surface: In Sweden someone recalls putting away a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocking back' is a drinker's phrase that doubles as the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Wine is an alcoholic beverage made from fermented grapes, a typical drink.

clue.text: Frightened son leaving to be looked after

indicators.note: when someone is leaving they go away, so that letter departs from the word

explanation.surface: A frightened boy leaves home to be taken into care.
explanation.definitionFit: To care for someone is to look after them, so cared and looked after are past forms with the same sense.

clue.text: Big shot getting bowled out in haste

indicators.note: out means removed, as a dismissed batsman leaves the field

blocks.note: a big shot is a celebrity
B is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for bowled

explanation.surface: A star batsman is bowled out in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket scoring, b stands for bowled.
explanation.definitionFit: Celerity is a formal word for speed or swiftness, so it is a synonym of haste.

clue.text: Salmon provided by shop in Kensington

indicators.note: the letters are supplied by the words that follow, sitting within them

explanation.surface: Fish bought from a shop in a smart London district.
explanation.walkthrough: Salmon looks like the fish but is the colour; Kensington is an upmarket area of west London.
explanation.definitionFit: Salmon is a pale orange-pink shade, so it is a kind of pink.

clue.text: Mountain climbing? Time for mega-stand

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing means going upwards, so the letters read bottom to top

blocks.note: M is the symbol for the prefix mega

explanation.surface: A mountaineer is told it is time for a huge stand.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen in 'mega-stand' glues the definition to the wordplay; M is the SI symbol for mega, a million.
explanation.definitionFit: A platform is a raised level surface on which people or things stand.

clue.text: Persuades wife to pay attention to Dennis

blocks.note: to heed is to pay attention to

explanation.surface: Someone coaxes his wife into listening to a man called Dennis.
explanation.walkthrough: Dennis is a surname here: Les Dennis is a British comedian who presented the game show Family Fortunes.
explanation.definitionFit: To wheedle is to coax or cajole someone into doing something, so it means to persuade.

clue.text: Britain had one politician detained by Ireland

indicators.note: someone detained is held within, so this piece is kept inside the other

blocks.note: Éire is the Irish name for Ireland

explanation.surface: A British politician is held in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a whole phrase: Britain once had an empire.
explanation.definitionFit: The British Empire was the vast collection of territories ruled by Britain.

clue.text: Asian state content to leave ludicrous targets

indicators.note: the content of a word is its inside, so once it leaves only the outer letters stay

blocks.note: Goa is a state of India
the first and last letters of ludicrous

explanation.surface: An Asian nation is happy to abandon absurd aims.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Asian state' tempts a country; it is a state within India.
explanation.definitionFit: Goals are aims or objectives one strives for, which are targets.

clue.text: Relative managed to break into key US city

indicators.note: breaking into something means getting inside it, so this piece goes within the others

blocks.note: to run a business is to manage it

explanation.surface: A family member was able to break into a big American city using a key.
explanation.definitionFit: A granny is a grandmother, a family relative.

clue.text: USA proven to distress star having a meltdown

indicators.note: distress means to put out of shape, so these letters are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: America is shown to upset a celebrity who throws a tantrum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Star having a meltdown' suggests a diva's tantrum; it is a literal exploding star.
explanation.definitionFit: A supernova is a star that explodes catastrophically at the end of its life.

clue.text: Playwright was upset about ending of Macbeth

indicators.note: the ending is the final part, so only the closing letter of the play's name is used
about means surrounding, so the verb goes around the single letter
in a down entry, upset means turned upside down, so the letters read bottom to top

explanation.surface: A dramatist was distressed by how Macbeth finishes.
explanation.walkthrough: George Bernard Shaw, Irish playwright; fittingly he also wrote The Apple Cart, in a puzzle themed on apples.
explanation.definitionFit: George Bernard Shaw was an Irish dramatist, author of plays such as Pygmalion.

clue.text: Mountain tops in France, usually just ice

indicators.note: the tops of words are their first letters, taken from each word that follows

blocks.note: the first letter of each word

explanation.surface: Mountain summits in France are usually nothing but ice.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount Fuji is the highest peak in Japan, a volcanic mountain.

clue.text: European agreement on snoring being music

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece on another sits above it, so it is written first

blocks.note: ZZ is the cartoon sound of snoring

explanation.surface: A European nods off and snores along to some music.
explanation.definitionFit: Jazz is a genre of popular music originating in African-American communities.

clue.text: Repeats one's rights during revolting arrest

indicators.note: revolting here means turning over, so the word for arrest is read backwards
something that happens during an event occurs within it, so these letters sit inside

blocks.note: one is A; the 's stands for has
R is right, so two rights

explanation.surface: A detainee keeps repeating their rights during a violent arrest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's' is read as 'one has', a common linking trick, so the rights simply follow the A.
explanation.definitionFit: To parrot is to repeat words mechanically without understanding, as the bird mimics speech.

clue.text: No longer held fun rave with zero dancing

indicators.note: to rave is to rant wildly, so the word before it is jumbled
dancing letters move about, so the word before it is rearranged

explanation.surface: Restrictions lift, allowing a fun rave with nobody dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rave' and 'dancing' look like a party scene, but each one scrambles the word just before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Frozen assets or prices are held fixed; once they are unfrozen they are released, no longer held.
